response.title: which projector screen for an ultra short throw projector is the best value
response.answer:
For an ultra-short-throw (UST) projector, the best value is usually a 100-inch fixed-frame ALR screen designed specifically for UST projectors, rather than a regular projector screen.

The key is to look for lenticular ALR (ambient light rejecting) or CLR (ceiling light rejecting) material. These screens reject overhead light while reflecting the projector's light toward your seating position.

My recommendation depends mainly on your room:

Dark room: A regular matte-white screen can save hundreds of dollars and still look excellent.

Living room with some ambient light: A budget UST ALR screen is usually the sweet spot.

Bright room with daytime viewing: A higher-quality UST ALR screen becomes worth paying for.

One important warning: Avoid ordinary ALR screens designed for long-throw projectors. They can perform poorly with UST projectors.

103-inch CLR2. Established manufacturer, UST-specific material, and a modest price premium over the budget pick.

Elite Screens - Aeon CLR 3 Series 103" Fixed Frame - Black

$728.00

103-inch CLR3. Worth considering if you want to spend more for a UST-specific screen from an established brand.

AWOL Vision - 100" Fixed Frame Projector Screen, 4K/8K UHD A…

$269.00

100-inch matte white, not ALR. Best for a dark room where ambient-light rejection isn't necessary.

My pick: The NothingProjector PET Crystal at around $399 is the strongest budget candidate. If the Elite Screens CLR2 is available for $549, I'd lean toward the Elite for its established brand and relatively small price difference. These are value judgments based on specifications and pricing, not a direct side-by-side test.
